security_audit.summary: All 19 static findings are false positives from a documentation-and-reference skill. The flagged patterns are standard open-source contributor instructions (uv installer, .env.example setup, os.environ API-key reads) and a well-secured client-side memory tool whose shutil operations are confined by path validation. No data-exfiltration, prompt-injection, or malicious intent was found; the only genuine issue is a SKILL.md frontmatter that cannot be statically parsed because a 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line precedes the YAML block.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md frontmatter is not machine-parseable: a plaintext line ('TRANSLATED CONTENT:') appears before the opening '---' YAML delimiter, so the metadata block cannot be extracted by automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line so the file begins directly with the '---' frontmatter delimiter. Apply the same cleanup to reference files that carry the same translation-pipeline prefix.

remediation.issue: The CONTRIBUTING.md quick start pipes a remote install script directly into a shell (curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh), which is a documentation example rather than executed skill code.
remediation.suggestion: Optionally note the pinned-version or checksum-verified install alternative alongside the pipe-to-shell command so readers who copy it can choose a safer path. This is advisory only; the command targets the trusted astral.sh domain.

content.user_title: Build Apps with the Claude API Cookbook
content.value_statement: Developers often struggle to find correct, current patterns for Claude API features like tool use, vision, and prompt caching. This skill provides copy-ready code examples and best practices sourced from the official Anthropic cookbooks, so you can integrate Claude quickly and correctly.
actual_capabilities: Provides working Python examples for basic Claude API messages, tool use, vision, and prompt caching.
Explains how to implement Retrieval Augmented Generation, classification, summarization, and text-to-SQL patterns.
Includes a secure, path-validated reference implementation of the client-side memory tool.
Documents best practices for model selection, prompt engineering, and cost optimization.
Organizes reference material by feature area, including tool use, multimodal, and third-party integrations.
limitations: The included Python examples reference older model identifiers and should be updated to current model names before production use.
It provides reference documentation and code samples, not an installable library or runnable application.
Coverage focuses on common patterns and does not include every Claude API feature or edge case.
The memory tool implementation is a client-side example that requires your own storage configuration.

use_cases.title: Learn Claude API integration
use_cases.description: A developer new to the Claude API uses the quick reference and code examples to make a first successful API call and understand core message structure.
use_cases.target_user: Developers new to the Claude API

use_cases.title: Implement tool use and agents
use_cases.description: An engineer building an AI agent references the tool use patterns to define tool schemas, handle tool results, and structure the agentic loop correctly.

use_cases.title: Add a persistent memory backend
use_cases.description: A team adopting Claude memory features studies the secure memory tool handler to implement path validation and safe file operations in their own storage layer.

prompt_templates.title: Make a first API call
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the simplest example of sending a message to the Claude API and reading the text response.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a minimal working request.

prompt_templates.title: Define and use a tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a weather tool schema and handle the tool use response from Claude.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is adding function calling to their application.

prompt_templates.title: Add prompt caching
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to add prompt caching to a request that reuses a large system prompt across many calls.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants to reduce cost for repeated context.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a secure memory backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Walk me through implementing a path-validated memory tool handler that prevents directory traversal, and explain each security control.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer is building a production memory storage layer.

output_examples.input: Show me the simplest example of sending a message to the Claude API.
output_examples.output: The skill provides a minimal Python snippet that creates a client, sends a single user message with a model and token limit, and reads the text back from the response content. It also explains that you must check the block type before accessing the text field.

output_examples.input: How do I define a tool for Claude to call?
output_examples.output: The skill shows how to build a tool definition with a name, description, and JSON schema for inputs. It then explains how to detect a tool use block in the response, execute the tool, and return the result so the conversation can continue.

best_practices: Choose the model that fits the task: a balanced model for most work, a faster model for simple or latency-sensitive tasks.
Read credentials from environment variables and never hardcode API keys in source code.
Validate and confine every file path in tool handlers to a fixed root to prevent directory traversal.
anti_patterns: Do not copy older model identifiers from the examples into production without updating them to current model names.
Do not access the text field of a response block without first checking the block type.
Do not skip path validation when implementing the memory tool, because it exposes the filesystem to traversal attacks.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides reference documentation and code examples for building applications with the Claude API, including tool use, vision, retrieval augmented generation, and prompt caching.

faq.question: Is this a runnable library or an application?
faq.answer: No. It is a collection of documentation and code samples. You copy the patterns into your own project rather than installing it as a package.

faq.question: Which programming language do the examples use?
faq.answer: The code examples use Python with the official Anthropic Python SDK. The patterns translate to other official SDKs as well.

faq.question: Are the model names in the examples current?
faq.answer: Some examples reference older model identifiers. You should replace them with current model names before using the code in production.

faq.question: Is the memory tool implementation safe to use?
faq.answer: The included handler applies path validation to prevent directory traversal and confines all operations to a memory root directory. You still configure your own storage location and review it for your environment.

faq.question: Does this skill make network requests on its own?
faq.answer: No. The network references in the documentation are setup instructions and example code. The reference material itself does not perform hidden network calls.
